To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphogen-based mechanism of driver cells self-generation preserves evolvability of large and complex structures.

(i) the separation between normal cells and driver cell is sufficient for the evolution of very large complex multicellular structures; (ii) the density of driver cells is a crucial parameter for evolvability; and (iii) the mechanism based on morphogens allows for generation of driver cells in a self-consistent manner.
the separation of cells into drivers and normal cells allows for the evolution of very complex structures and that the separation is preserved by the morphogen-based generation of driver cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of complex structures in a model of Artificial Life that uses Artificial Embryology as a development engine.
evolution of complex structures in the context of Artificial Embryologies.
understanding how to evolve complex structures in a way similar to how they evolved in nature, by combining the principles of Artificial Embryogenesis with the methods of Artificial Evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Epigenetic Tracking, with its ability to generate complex structures with millions of normal cells, is a promising approach for Artificial Embryology.
Epigenetic Tracking with drivers generated by morphogens is a promising approach to the evolution of large complex artificial structures with millions of elements.
Epigenetic Tracking with drivers generated from a morphogen field is a promising model of artificial embryogenesis for the study of multicellular evolution and development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the separation of cells into drivers and normal cells, and the use of morphogen-based generation of driver cells allows to evolve structures with millions of normal cells and hundreds of drivers, and that this mechanism is a promising starting point for evolution of structures that are robust to damage and to developmental noise.
Epigenetic Tracking provides a framework for the evolution of complex multicellular structures with a high number of cells.

we have shown that evolution of large complex structures with millions of components is feasible, and we have shown how this evolution may be extended to include robustness to damage and to developmental noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the separation between normal cells and driver-cells, which was originally introduced to facilitate the evolution of large and complex multicellular structures, can be used to build a robust developmental system.

the separation of driver cells from normal cells allows for the evolution of complex structures with much higher number of normal cells than in other Artificial Evolution models, while preserving the evolvability and robustness to noise.
morphogens can provide a robust mechanism for self-generation of evolving driver cells.
